$comment: Evaluation weights for evaluateLightState() in ai.ts.
SCALE: one average unit on the board is worth ~10000 ('unit.presence' plus
its type/stat terms). Every other term is expressed as a fraction of that,
so a positional bonus can never silently outweigh losing a piece. Before
this file the numbers were inline literals on no common scale: a 3 hp
difference (3000) outscored perfect archer spacing (1500) by 2x for no
stated reason.
ARMOR IS A CONSUMABLE SHIELD, not a damage reducer. combat.ts
applyDamageToTarget zeroes armor the moment damage exceeds it, so a point
of armor absorbs damage roughly once. That is why armor is priced well
below hp here (the old code had armor at half of hp, far too high).
HP IS TINY (units have 2-5 hp) and damage is large (3-7). Almost every
connecting attack is lethal or near-lethal, so threat/hanging terms matter
more than in a game with big hp pools -- but they must stay below the
value of the unit itself or the bot refuses to trade at all.

material.$comment: Core piece value. presence is the flat 'a unit exists' term that dominates every positional consideration.

castle.$comment: Castle capture is the real win condition; these dwarf material on purpose.

focus.$comment: Bonus for enemies already wounded, so damage concentrates instead of spreading.

retreat.$comment: When outnumbered, pull back toward home. Scales with the size of the deficit.

spacing.$comment: Per-unit-type ideal distance to the nearest enemy. Ranged kite, melee close.

$comment: Threat used to be counted three times over (opponentThreatWeight, the
hanging-piece pass, and indirectly via spacing), with one of the three
uncapped. These are the single source of truth now; hangingMax caps the
total so a threatened unit is never worth more than losing it outright.

cohesion.$comment: Penalty per unit with no friendly unit within `radius`.

$comment: NEW in v2. evaluateLightState previously had no inventory term at all,
so MCTS saw 'draw' (search ruins) as an action costing the unit's whole
activation for zero evaluated gain, and crafting as pure loss. The whole
economy layer was effectively off, most visibly on `hard` where
trustSearch keeps the search plan verbatim.
Artifacts are priced by rarity from RUINS_LOOT_TABLE weights (5/3/3/2/2
out of 100) and by how many recipes need them. Values stay modest: an
artifact is a fraction of a unit, because holding one wins nothing by
itself -- it has to be spent.
economy.$comment_recipe: Extra credit once a full recipe is affordable -- a complete set is worth far more than the sum of its parts, since that is the point at which it converts into stats.
economy.$comment_ruins: Pull toward the ruins so units actually go farm when nothing better is happening. Deliberately small: it must never outweigh a capture or a kill.
economy.$comment_gear: Equipped gear is already reflected in unit damage/armor, so this only prices the standing option value of unspent kit.

buffs.$comment: Active spell effects on the light state (shieldTurns / damageBuff).

tempo.$comment: Side-to-move terms (t = +1 when it is my move, -1 otherwise), each multiplying a threat sum. 0 here keeps the beam search unchanged; chance-weights.json fits them.

$comment: Rollout policy shaping. The greedy playout assumes BOTH sides always take
the locally best action, which models a human badly -- humans set up
trades and sacrifices that a greedy simulation never predicts, so any
line depending on the opponent's reply is mis-evaluated.
opponentNoiseChance makes the simulated opponent occasionally take its
2nd/3rd-best action instead, widening the distribution of replies the
search prices in. 0 restores the fully-greedy behaviour.
MEASURED, and the theory LOST: on the 'beats a greedy opponent' game test
noise 0 wins 3/3, noise 0.25 wins 2/3, noise 0.10 wins 1/3. Same lesson as
the RAVE experiment -- a standard MCTS improvement that does not survive
contact with this game. The mechanism is that the light-state rollout is
already a coarse approximation, so extra variance on top of it degrades
the value estimate faster than it buys robustness to non-greedy replies.
Kept implemented but OFF; raise it only alongside a fresh measurement.
